items.summary: Timed blocks start with everything on screen on a phone. Coding: the table of shapes is one bordered reference strip of nine borderless cells (no tile looks like a key; glyph 1.25rem, never wider than its column), the target is 6rem below 30rem, the keypad is one row of nine keys (Keypad gets an optional `columns` prop; keys keep 2.75rem height and give up width, min 24 px), and start() scrolls the table to the top of the screen before focusing the stage with preventScroll. Digit span, RT and Corsi focus their stage through a new `focusStage` (focus with preventScroll, then scrollIntoView nearest). Key + target + keypad measure about 310 px (budget 468).

items.summary: Matrix options are drawn at the size of a grid cell: OptionGroup gets `flush` (card with no padding or border, a box-shadow frame outside the figure; chosen = 4 px frame + inverted letter) and `maxWidth`; the matrix lays options out as two rows of three with the same width cap as the grid (both read --grid-max = 22.5rem, same 0.5rem gap, both align-self flex-start), so each option track is exactly a grid track. Measured: option svg and grid svg widths equal at 1280, 768, 390 and 320 px; grid and options share their left edge and width. draw.ts untouched.

items.summary: OptionGroup: Confirm is `hb-btn hb-primary` (its own button rules deleted; the form is `choice hb-render` and imports render.css so the shared rules and tokens apply on any page); option cards focus with the same amber 3 px ring as every control (offset 2 px, 4 px on flush cards); disabled Confirm gets the shared disabled look (opacity 0.6). A repeat of an earlier touch tap is held back: a touch tap within 350 ms of the group appearing, at the spot (32 px) of a touch tap made before it appeared (600 ms), selects nothing and leaves the radio as it was; mouse, pen, keyboard and any other tap are never held back.

items.notes: DEVIATION from the triage's guard: 'a touch tap < 350 ms after mount' as specified swallows the SessionDriver's taps in the iphone project (measured: its option taps land 57 to 131 ms after the group mounts, and `tick()` then fails with 'unchecked'; the triage assumed the drivers click). The guard therefore also requires the tap to repeat the spot of an earlier touch tap made before the group appeared, which is the double-tap tail itself. The whole touch-driven session (e2e/session-save.spec.ts 'plays from the start page', iphone) passes with it. `--hb-focus` is kept (value now the amber #b45309 / #fbbf24 of --r-focus, instead of being dropped) because scripts/contrast.test.ts pairs --hb-focus, --hb-card-border, --hb-chosen and --hb-surface of OptionGroup by name; dropping it would fail that test. Snapshots of OptionGroup users changed only by the Svelte class hash. A module-level pointerdown listener (capture, passive) in OptionGroup.svelte records the last two touch presses.

items.summary: Corsi blocks are placed by their centres (--x/--y/--s custom properties, left/top = centre, translate(-50%,-50%)) with width and height max(size%, 2.75rem), so they are at least 44 px on any board while their centres keep the fractions; the board is min(100%, 26rem, 52vh) (52svh where supported); the gaps to the status line and Undo/Done are 0.5rem. Measured at 390 x 664 and 320 x 568: nine blocks >= 44 x 44, none overlap, all inside the board, and with the h1 at the top of the screen Undo and Done end inside the first screen. tasks/span/config.ts untouched.

items.summary: NumericEntry normalises the typed text before accepts/submit (new common/normalize-digits.ts): NFKC, the digits of Arabic-Indic, Extended Arabic-Indic and Devanagari to ASCII, and inner white space (spaces, U+00A0, U+202F, tabs) removed when the text is only a sign, digits and a point (so '1 000' is 1000 but the mixed number '2 1/3' keeps its spaces); fractions get the digit mapping only, letters nothing; the ASCII text is what onsubmit and the family's parser receive. Decimal entries get a point key ('Decimal point', translate=no) beside the sign key when the browser language writes decimals with a comma or the pointer is coarse, inserting at the caret. QuantRenderer: an integer item accepts only whole values ('3.5', '7/2' get the integer note). entry-copy notes reworded as in the triage. Entry box flex 0 1 12rem / max 12rem (fraction keeps its width).

items.notes: NEEDS INTEGRATION: scripts/contrast.test.ts 'every colour token of src/ sits in a rule that a sheet above stands for' compares t.media to the exact string '@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)', so it now fails for the render.css tokens (and for src/brief/notes.css and src/brief/ui/ResultsTalk.svelte, which other packages moved to the same `screen and` form). See integration_requests. No new colour token or literal was added.

integration_requests.change: Line 212 `const DARK = '@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)'` and line 222 `t.media !== DARK`: accept the print-safe form too, e.g. `const DARK = new Set(['@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)', '@media screen and (prefers-color-scheme: dark)'])` and `!DARK.has(t.media)`. scripts/css-tokens.ts and the 'a dark-scheme rule is not undone by a later rule' test already match both forms (their regexes are /prefers-color-scheme:\s*dark/). Until then `npm test` has exactly this one failure; it lists src/render/common/render.css (this package) and src/brief/notes.css and src/brief/ui/ResultsTalk.svelte (other packages).

Optional clean-up only: OptionGroup.svelte keeps the token --hb-focus (now amber, the same hex as --r-focus) because the pair('--hb-focus', '--hb-surface', ...) at line 137 names it. If the integrator wants the token gone (the triage said 'drop --hb-focus'), delete that pair and the --hb-focus lines in OptionGroup.svelte's .choice rule and its dark override, and use var(--r-focus) in the two outline rules. Not needed for green gates.

Optional wording only: the `state` of the route 'item-spatial-no-webgl' still says 'the notice, the text alternatives and the skip offer'; without WebGL the renderer now draws only the one-line notice (the skip offer is the session's .unavailable group). The route's assertions (.unavailable, 'Skip Spatial') still hold.
